source.title: Generalization Error Bounds of Gradient Descent for Learning Over-Parameterized Deep ReLU Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some mathematical symbols and equations are garbled in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves algorithm-dependent generalization results for over-parameterized deep ReLU networks using theoretical bounds, a different method from the empirical tests described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites empirical random-label fitting from Zhang et al. (2017), but does not test random-label fitting itself. Its own results are theoretical guarantees under stated data assumptions; no experimental outcomes are reported.
record.test_reason: The paper proves conditional population-error guarantees for deep fully connected ReLU networks. It does not establish V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization for the same training recipe. Its width-dependent error bounds also do not establish V2's decrease in actual test error beyond interpolation. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under either of two distributional separability assumptions, sufficient width and sample size, and prescribed initialization and optimization conditions, GD finds an iterate with arbitrarily small population classification error. The proved setting is binary classification with deep fully connected ReLU networks and cross-entropy loss.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes fully connected deep ReLU networks trained with full-batch gradient descent from Gaussian initialization and cross-entropy loss. Its results are theoretical guarantees under distributional assumptions, rather than the empirical random-label memorization experiments described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on the data-distribution assumption, depth, margin, width, sample size, initialization, step size, and confidence parameter.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollaries 4.11 and 4.13 guarantee population classification accuracy at least 1 − ε for sufficiently wide deep ReLU networks trained by GD, given sufficient samples and either of two margin-separability assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified distributional separability assumptions, sufficiently wide deep fully connected ReLU networks trained from Gaussian initialization by GD can achieve arbitrarily small population classification error.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 4.9 contains a width-dependent term decreasing as m^(-1/6), under its optimization assumptions. A decreasing upper bound does not establish decreasing actual test error beyond interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated gradient lower bound and training conditions, increasing width improves a term in a population-error upper bound.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and conditional on assumptions, including separability by a random ReLU feature or by the conjugate kernel. The paper reports no empirical validation of these guarantees and does not test random-label fitting.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results met the row criteria for the tested version; the remaining claim versions are not tested.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; the paper cites this empirical phenomenon rather than establishing it.
Actual test-error changes as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The discussion following Corollary 4.9 states that independent Rademacher labels imply population error cannot fall below 1/2. This does not establish that the same recipe fits those random labels, so it does not complete a test of V1. No empirical experiments are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels, compare random-label and natural-label training, or report empirical results on the named architectures and datasets. It establishes theoretical generalization guarantees for deep fully connected ReLU networks under particular separability assumptions.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.operation_detail: Theorem guarantees a population classification error bound under Assumption 4.10, separability by a random ReLU feature.

conditions.value: Assumption 4.10: separable by a random ReLU feature with margin γ
gradient descent with step size η = O(4^-L L^-3 γ^2 m^-1)
n ≥ n*(ε, L, γ, δ) as stated in Corollary 4.11
m ≥ m*(ε, L, γ, δ) as stated in Corollary 4.11

rows.value: At least 1 − ε, with probability at least 1 − δ
rows.note: The theorem is a theoretical guarantee for the stated distributional assumption, not an empirical measurement.
rows.check: Corollary 4.11 correctly guarantees population accuracy at least 1 − ε under random-ReLU-feature separability, but this is a conditional theorem, not an observed outcome. It does not establish random-label fitting or the paired comparison required by V1. The guarantee concerns an iterate found within the stated iteration budget; normalized inputs and balanced layer widths are also assumed.
